page.layout: One column of running text, with a centred heading above the second passage. No marginal notes. Below the text, at the right, a catchword "Appa-".

main_text.p: fisse. Unde mirum non est singulas arbores bina millia nummûm annuo reditu meruisse, cum septem & sexaginta malaillam summam conficere potuerint, tricenis nummis singula venundata. De nucleis persicorum non pretereundum est ex oleo rosaceo, & aceto temperatos capitis dolores sedare, efitatos[?] autem tormina ventris. Flores saccharo conditi stomacho utiles sunt. Eligenda quae minus succulenta sunt perfica, quorumq; fissa caro ligno minime adhæret. Succosa enim nimis damnantur.
main_text.head: De cucumere, cucurbita, melone, pepone.

p.i: Melonum, peponum, cucumerum, cucurbitarumq; varia genera nouit Italia & Gallia, quorum plerasq; in Germaniam nunc quoq; nostram commigrarunt. Non enim indiligenter in hortis excoluntur, expetuntur enim tum à magnatibus, tum à pauperibus, non sine valetudinis sæpe incommodo. Calidioris enim temperaturæ hominibus, & ab ineunte ætate iis assuetis magis conueniunt, frigido humidoq; ventriculo incommodant. Semina vero omnium in renum vesicaq; affectib. ut stranguria, calculo &c. valde commendantur.
(Cucurbita in cibos decoquuntur, cruda enim non estur, fatua siquidem & insipida sunt.

page.notes: The first paragraph is a continuation from the previous page. The title "De cucumere..." is set as a centred heading and is treated as level 2. The word "efitatos" is doubtful (possibly "efficatos"), so it is marked [?]. The initial M is a large woodcut-style initial joined to "Elonum" as "Melonum". The running head is printed in small capitals. Some ligatures and letter forms are uncertain; the transcription follows the visible letters.
